chunks: Because they followed what displeased God, and they were averse to pleasing Him. So We nullified their deeds.
ai.seo_question: Why were the deeds of the hypocrites nullified according to Surah Muhammad?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the specific group of hypocrites or those who outwardly professed faith but inwardly rejected the truth, particularly emphasizing the rejection of the Ahl al-Bayt as a manifestation of 'disliking God's pleasure.' The nullification (ihbat) of their deeds is not merely a punishment but a natural consequence of their internal contradiction, where their actions lacked the essential core of sincerity (ikhlas) and alignment with divine will. This highlights the Shia principle that true acceptance of God's pleasure is intrinsically tied to accepting the guidance of the Imams.
